title: Moth Demonstrates Topology-Aware Quantum Data Encoding Across 120 Qubits Without SWAP Overhead - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Moth Quantum's Tessa scheme 2-colors IBM chip coupling graphs into address/data registers to load up to 1,568 real values across a 120-qubit Nighthawk processor with no SWAPs or ancillas, beating QCrank's 128-value record without error mitigation. Sampling cost grows exponentially with local connectivity, so it targets low-degree QML feature ingestion; Moth is shipping it via its Atlas creative platform.

insights.claim: Moth Quantum's Tessa (Tessellated QPIXL) state-preparation scheme encodes and retrieves up to 1,568 real-valued parameters across every qubit of an IBM Quantum processor without SWAP routing gates or ancilla qubits.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Signals software-side gains in usable qubit capacity for data loading on existing IBM hardware, a key QML bottleneck.
insights.quote: encodes and retrieves up to 1,568 real-valued parameters across every qubit of an IBM Quantum processor without SWAP routing gates or ancilla qubits

insights.claim: Conventional quantum angle/amplitude encoders such as QPIXL and QCrank depend on uniformly controlled rotations needing all-to-all star connectivity, which forces deep SWAP chains on nearest-neighbor superconducting chips.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Data-loading cost on nearest-neighbor hardware is dominated by routing overhead; schemes that avoid it gain a practical edge.
insights.quote: forcing deep SWAP chains on nearest-neighbor superconducting chips

insights.claim: Tessa 2-colors the physical device coupling graph into interleaved address and data registers so each data qubit runs a multiplexer controlled only by adjacent address qubits, making circuit depth depend on local vertex degree rather than total chip size.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Hardware-native, topology-matched compilation lets encoding scale with chip size without depth blowup — a design pattern worth watching across quantum software.
insights.quote: yielding a circuit depth governed by local vertex degree rather than total chip size

insights.claim: On the 120-qubit IBM Nighthawk r2 (ibm_phoenix) square lattice, Tessa encoded 784 values in 728 CZ gates (depth 23) in single Z-basis mode, achieving 0.075 MAE and 0.96 correlation after contrast recovery.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Concrete fidelity metrics on IBM's newest square-lattice chip show useful data loading is feasible today without error mitigation.

insights.claim: In phase-pair mode (Z and X bases) on IBM Nighthawk r2, Tessa encoded 1,568 values in 1,456 CZ gates (depth 43), with 0.154 value MAE and 0.092 hue MAE at 8,192 shots per basis — doubling capacity at the cost of roughly double depth and higher error.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Shows the capacity/accuracy trade-off in two-basis encoding; error roughly doubles as capacity doubles.

insights.claim: On the 156-qubit IBM Heron r2 (ibm_fez) heavy-hex processor, Tessa encoded 441 values (428 CZ gates, 0.95 correlation) in Z mode and 882 values (852 CZ gates) in pair mode — fewer than on the 120-qubit square lattice despite more qubits.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Topology matters as much as qubit count for data-loading capacity; IBM's shift to square-lattice Nighthawk appears to benefit such workloads.

insights.claim: Without quantum error mitigation, Tessa surpassed the 128-value hardware record previously set by QCrank for encoding arbitrary real-valued vectors on quantum hardware.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: More than an order-of-magnitude jump over the prior record marks Moth as a notable player in quantum data-encoding IP.
insights.quote: surpassed the 128-value hardware record previously set by QCrank for arbitrary real-valued vectors

insights.claim: Using Bloch-sphere constellation encoding at 32,768 shots, Tessa recovered 92.3% of a 784-nucleotide MT-CO3 DNA sequence and 71.5% of a 393-amino-acid p53 protein sequence.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Early demonstration of biological-sequence loading, relevant to quantum-for-life-sciences narratives, though recovery is imperfect.

insights.claim: Because readout shots split across the 2^m local address states of a degree-m data qubit, Tessa's sampling overhead scales exponentially with local connectivity, positioning it for low-degree QML feature ingestion rather than general-purpose classical memory.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Temper expectations: this is a QML feature-loading tool, not a path to quantum RAM; higher-connectivity chips would raise shot costs.
insights.quote: positioning Tessa for low-degree QML feature ingestion rather than general-purpose classical memory
insights.locator: The author notes that because readout shots

insights.claim: Moth Quantum has made Tessa available inside Atlas, its alpha-stage creative and developer platform serving thousands of early users across music, gaming, and visual media, accessible via no-code web engines and APIs targeting quantum hardware and emulators.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Moth is monetizing quantum research through creative-industry tooling rather than waiting for fault-tolerant advantage — an unusual go-to-market to track.
insights.quote: alpha-stage creative and developer platform serving thousands of early users across music, gaming, and visual media

insights.claim: Atlas pairs Tessa image processing with quantum-driven creative utilities including a quantum audio re-encoder, MIDI variation generator, Quantum Blur, Entanglement Shader, Telablur image morphing, and hardware-seeded maze generation; the Tessa code is open-sourced on GitHub.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Open-source plus creative apps suggests a community/developer-adoption strategy over enterprise sales.
